paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Psalm 36 puts two pictures side by side. One man is so full of himself that he can't spot his own sin, let alone hate it (Psalm 36:2). Then David turns to the LORD, and the whole view changes. The wicked man's world is as small as a schemer's bedroom, and God's loving devotion "reaches to the heavens" (Psalm 36:5).

So what does that teach us? The wicked man isn't missing information. He's missing the fear of God, and that's where everything starts to go wrong (Psalm 36:1). But God isn't far off and stingy. David says people take refuge in the shadow of His wings, feast on the abundance of His house, and drink from His river of delights (Psalm 36:7-8). I can't even keep a straight face about the chocolate chips, and God is handing out a RIVER.

And here's why it matters to you. "For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light" (Psalm 36:9). We don't see clearly by staring at ourselves, we see clearly by looking to Him. So David ends in prayer: "Extend Your loving devotion to those who know You…" (Psalm 36:10). That's a good prayer to bake into your day, baker, because you don't have to climb to the clouds to find His love. It already reaches there.
